messages:
ashley: Quick heads-up — saw ~8-12% latency regression on streaming paths when continuous-batcher + kernel auto-switch enabled on 2.2.0-gpu. Repro steps below. :thinking:
ashley: Repro: send ~1200 concurrent streams, avg 60 tokens, model rwd-v1-13b, stream=true, token_budget=256, kernel_selector=auto
ashley: Logs show repeated "kernel-evict->kernel-load" handoffs during partial-decode windows, and KV cache warmups triggering flushes.
ashley: Profiler snippet:
```
timeline: decode_start -> partial_decode_wait 40ms -> kernel_switch 18ms -> flush_tx 12ms -> resume_decode
hotspots:
- kv_cache_miss: 23%
- kernel_load: 19%
- stream_flush: 15%
```
miguel: ugh. do we have correlation with batch size? looks like micro-batches of 1-2 tokens causing kernel churn.
priya: @ashley can you attach the small perf trace? also which quant profile? q4_0?
ashley: yes q4_0. stack shows kernel selector picks tiny-kernel for short seqs then switches to large-kernel mid-stream when KV cache warms.
ben: could be our heuristic: we pick kernel based on predicted final seq length (from prompt + history) but streaming adds tokens unpredictably.
joanna: suggestion: add hysteresis in kernel selection — require sustained token-rate or batch-length before switching.
miguel: also queue policy: admission currently favors latency so it flushes tiny batches early; streaming + small early flushes hurt amortization.
ashley: proposed quick experiment:
- disable kernel auto-switch for streamed requests
- increase token_budget target from 256 -> 512 for streams
- set stream_flush_cooldown = 30ms
ashley: CLI to toggle:
```
rwctl set runtime kernel.autoswitch.stream false
rwctl set runtime batching.token_budget.stream 512
rwctl set runtime batching.stream_cooldown_ms 30
```
sre-bot: deploy triggered by @ashley: rolling config change to canary pool rg-stream-canary
sre-bot: canary done 4/10 instances, monitoring for 5m
ben: after canary: p50 latency down 6%, p95 down 10%, but GPU CPU on nodes increased ~4%
priya: any impact on non-streaming workloads?
ashley: non-streaming unchanged in initial runs. we'll run additional qps sweep.
joanna: for longer term: consider kernel selection tied to batch eligibility window rather than predicted seq length. also cache-warm flags to avoid kernel reloads mid-decode.
miguel: can we make partial-decode schedule preemptive: if kernel switch is predicted within next 50 tokens, delay switch until flush boundary to avoid stalls.
ashley: filed PERF-4321 with trace and experiment results. TL;DR: streaming + continuous-batch heuristics need either larger token_budget or disabled kernel autoswitch + small cooldown for acceptable p95.
ben: FYI I recorded flamegraph and saved to s3://redwood-perf/streams/2155123456/flame.svg
priya: next steps: 1) prod canary ramp 10% 2) run stream-heavy regression test 3) bake changes if stable
joanna: I'll prototype kernel hysteresis today, ping when PR is up :hammer:
ashley: thanks all :thumbsup:
